title: Domatic number

problem.name: Domatic number
problem.statement_latex:
Given $G=(V,E)$, maximize $k$ such that $V$ can be partitioned into $D_1,\ldots,D_k$ with $N[D_i]=V$ for every $i$. Each class is a dominating set. The problem models disjoint teams of resources, each capable of providing coverage to the entire network.
Quantum complexity is measured in QRAM time, classical inclusion--exclusion in RAM time, and the fixed-part-count Boolean algorithms in bit operations.

quantum.headline_latex: $O^*((2-\epsilon)^n)$ for some constant $\epsilon>0$, Gaspers--Li domatic-number algorithm.
quantum.details_latex: The theorem obtains a strict improvement below base two through restricted enumeration of minimal dominating sets and the covering framework. The analysis establishes the existence of $\epsilon$ rather than an optimized numerical base. The number of parts is optimized as part of the input problem, and preprocessing values are coherently accessible.
quantum.headline_text: $O^*((2-\epsilon)^n)$ for some constant $\epsilon>0$, Gaspers–Li domatic-number algorithm.
quantum.details_text: The theorem obtains a strict improvement below base two through restricted enumeration of minimal dominating sets and the covering framework. The analysis establishes the existence of $\epsilon$ rather than an optimized numerical base. classical.details_latex: For any fixed target $q$, the stronger bound is $O_{q,\eta}(2^{\eta n}\operatorname{poly}(n))$ for every fixed $\eta>0$. One-hot membership variables and closed-neighborhood domination clauses produce $O(qn)$ variables and $O(qn)$ possibly long clauses; long-clause shortening followed by fixed-width counting gives this bound. For fixed maximum degree, the same encoding has bounded width and linear size, yielding $\operatorname{poly}(n)2^{O_q(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$. These fixed-$q$ bounds do not treat an unbounded number of parts as a constant.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup through a smaller exponential constant for unrestricted domatic number, based on amplitude amplification. Fixed-$q$ decision has the subexponential classical comparison above.

evidence.description_latex: A rigorous quantum upper bound with partial evidence against the general classical exact algorithm. The fixed-$q$ classical conclusion follows the explicit domination encoding.

hardware.description_latex: Polynomial active subset and part-count registers accompany exponential coherent preprocessing memory. The small unspecified base improvement still entails exponentially long coherent searches on large graphs.
